recommendations.title: Shift Flexible Loads to Off-Peak
recommendations.detail: High demand is expected around 07:00, 08:00, 19:00, 20:00, 21:00. Move washing-machine cycles, dishwasher runs, and EV charging to off-peak windows (01:00-06:00) to reduce peak grid stress.

recommendations.title: Pre-condition HVAC Before Peak Windows
recommendations.detail: Sub-metering 3 (HVAC) is the largest flexible load. Start pre-cooling / pre-heating 30-60 minutes before 07:00, 08:00, 19:00, 20:00, 21:00 so the system can coast during the peak without full power draw.

recommendations.title: Pre-charge Storage During Off-Peak (01:00-06:00)
recommendations.detail: If a home battery or EV with V2H capability is available, schedule charging between 01:00 and 06:00 when average demand is lowest. Discharge during the predicted peak window (07:00, 08:00, 19:00, 20:00, 21:00) to reduce grid import and lower time-of-use tariff costs.

recommendations.title: Monitor Voltage During Peak Hours (07:00, 08:00, 19:00, 20:00, 21:00)
recommendations.detail: Target: 220.0-240.0 V. Historical out-of-band readings: 0.0% below 220.0 V, 64.65% above 240.0 V. Voltage sags often coincide with peak-demand periods - enable alerts on your smart meter or energy monitor.

recommendations.title: Review Time-of-Use Tariff Alignment
recommendations.detail: Peak demand clusters at 07:00, 08:00, 19:00, 20:00, 21:00. Check whether your energy supplier's peak tariff windows overlap with these hours. Even a 30-minute shift in large appliance usage can meaningfully reduce your monthly electricity bill.
